findings.title: No migration path for realms that already have the admin-permissions client provisioned before the Clients resource type was added
findings.body: init() exits immediately with `if (client != null) { return; }` whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. The new CLIENTS resource type and its scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite, etc.) are only created inside this method, which only runs once when the admin-permissions client is first provisioned. Any realm that already had Admin Fine-Grained Authorization V2 enabled before this change is deployed will keep an admin-permissions resource server that lacks these new scopes/resources forever, since init() will never run its resource/scope creation logic again. Subsequent attempts to create a Clients-type permission on such realms will fail deep inside getOrCreateResource with `ModelException("No scopes found.")` because the required scopes were never added to that resource server. There is no migration/upgrade logic in this PR to reconcile already-provisioned resource servers with the updated schema.

findings.title: Provider event listener now gated by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), silently skipping cleanup when only V2 is enabled
findings.body: The whole body of registerListener's onEvent was wrapped with `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`. However, `management()`/`evaluator()` elsewhere in this same file only check `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, and `AdminPermissionsSchema.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` also only checks the V2 feature — V2 can be enabled independently of V1. With this guard, realms that only enable ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (not the legacy V1 feature) will no longer process RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, or GroupRemovedEvent at all, whereas before this change they always were. This appears to have been added only to avoid calling the new ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), which throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the chosen fix disables event handling for roles and groups too (whose management() implementations are not overridden in V2 and would not have thrown). The consequence is that removing a role or group under a V2-only configuration no longer disables the associated permission state, leaving stale permission data behind.

findings.title: Incorrect Javadoc on void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes()
findings.body: The Javadoc added for `void requireView()` (line 98) says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", and the Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` (line 103) says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}". Both are void methods that throw ForbiddenException, not boolean-returning methods — this is a copy/paste error inconsistent with every other require*() method in the same interface (e.g. requireListClientScopes(), requireManage(), requireConfigure()), which correctly document the throwing behavior. This is misleading documentation for API consumers.

findings.title: getResourceName() was not updated to handle the new CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() only special-cases `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` to resolve a friendly name ("All users" for the blanket resource, or the username for an individual resource). No equivalent branch was added for CLIENTS, even though this PR introduces the Clients resource type and per-client resources (whose stored resource name is the client's internal ID, per resolveClient()). As a result, any permission representation built for a Clients-type policy falls through to `return resource.getDisplayName();`, which will surface the raw internal client ID (or the literal resource type name "Clients" for the blanket resource) instead of a human-readable name such as the client's clientId or "All clients", unlike the parity that exists for Users.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission() relies on resource type tagging that individually-created client resources never receive
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission() calls `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` to enumerate resources of type "Clients" and check granted scopes on each. However, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() (lines 101-111) creates per-object resources via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` without ever calling `resource.setType(...)`; only the single blanket/catch-all resource created in init() has its type explicitly set (`resource.setType(type)`). Because of this, individually-created per-client resources (e.g. the resource representing a single client granted MANAGE/VIEW) are not tagged with type "Clients" and will not be returned by findByType, so getClientsWithPermission will under-report clients that only have an individual (non-blanket) permission grant. There is also no test in this PR that exercises getClientsWithPermission with a per-client (non-'all') grant, so this gap would not be caught by CI.

findings.title: No test coverage for the map-roles-client-scope scope and ClientScopeModel-based permission checks added for Clients
findings.body: The PR adds the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope to the CLIENTS resource type and implements `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)`, as well as `canManage(ClientScopeModel)`/`canView(ClientScopeModel)` overrides used for realm-level client-scope management. None of the new tests in PermissionClientTest (or elsewhere in this PR) exercise canMapClientScopeRoles or the ClientScopeModel-based overrides (e.g. via the /client-scopes admin REST endpoints), unlike MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE which are all covered. This leaves a meaningful part of the new authorization logic unverified by automated tests.
